replies.What is your relationship with mathemati: Mathematics has always been a part of my life, even if I didn’t pursue it beyond high school. I find it calming to work through problems, especially when they’re connected to real-world applications like budgeting or cooking.

replies.How would you explain, step by step, how: First, write down the equation in standard form: ax² + bx + c = 0. Then use the quadratic formula: x equals negative b plus or minus square root of b squared minus four ac, all over two a. Plug in your values and simplify. If the discriminant is positive, you get two real solutions; if zero, one solution; if negative, complex ones.

To find stationary points, take the derivative of f(x), which gives you f'(x). Set f'(x) equal to zero and solve for x. These are your critical points. Then plug each value back into the original function to get the corresponding y-values. You can also use a graph to verify if they’re maxima or minima.
